title: Valley polarization, Rashba interaction, and weak altermagnetism in inversion-asymmetric MnPS$_\text{3}|$WS$_\text{2}$ van der Waals heterostructures
authors: Purba Dutta, Soumajyoti Bid, Nirmal Ganguli
abstract: The deliberate breaking of inversion ($\mathcal{P}$) symmetry in antiferromagnets has recently emerged as an effective means to induce various features, such as the emergence of Berry curvature, spin-valley locking, magnetoelectric coupling, and the transition from conventional antiferromagnetism to altermagnetism. Conversely, in non-magnetic systems, inversion symmetry breaking in the presence of strong spin-orbit interaction (SOI) gives rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting via the Rashba effect, enabling tunable spin polarization through external electric fields. Motivated by recent advances in two-dimensional materials, we perform first-principles calculations based on density functional theory to investigate the van der Waals (vdW) heterostructure formed by a $\mathcal{P}$-symmetric MnPS$_3$ monolayer and a WS$_2$ monolayer. We demonstrate that the interface hosts a rich interplay of emergent phenomena, including an altermagnetic phase, Rashba spin splitting, spin-valley locking, and valley polarization. Our results demonstrate that the heterostructure exhibits semiconducting behavior with a direct band gap of approximately 1.65~eV and a type-I band alignment. Remarkably, the electronic structure and band alignment can be effectively tuned between type-I and type-II regimes via an external electric field and in-plane biaxial strain. Furthermore, field-induced modulation enables strong control over the altermagnetic phase and the valley splitting. These findings establish the proposed vdW heterostructure as a highly tunable platform with significant potential for spintronic and valleytronic applications.
summary: This theoretical study investigates the $	ext{MnPS}_3|	ext{WS}_2$ van der Waals heterostructure to demonstrate its potential as a tunable platform. Using DFT, the authors show that the interface supports emergent phenomena like altermagnetism and Rashba splitting. Crucially, they prove that external electric fields and strain can reversibly tune the band alignment and control these quantum electronic states.
main_problem: Investigating emergent electronic and magnetic phenomena, such as altermagnetism, Rashba splitting, and spin-valley locking, in inversion-asymmetric van der Waals heterostructures.
main_result: The $	ext{MnPS}_3|	ext{WS}_2$ heterostructure exhibits a rich interplay of these effects, forming a highly tunable platform whose electronic properties can be controlled by external electric fields and strain.
method: First-principles calculations using Density Functional Theory (DFT) incorporating Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC) and DFT-D2 corrections for van der Waals interactions.
model_or_system: The physical system is a vdW heterostructure formed by stacking $	ext{MnPS}_3$ and $	ext{WS}_2$ monolayers. The study analyzes the electronic structure, magnetic ordering (altermagnetism), and spin-splitting effects at the interface.
key_observables: Electronic band gap ($\approx 1.65 	ext{ eV}$), type-I/type-II band alignment, Rashba spin splitting magnitude, valley polarization, and altermagnetic signatures.
important_parameters: External electric field (EEF) and in-plane biaxial strain are key tuning parameters; the system is analyzed near K and $ ar{	ext{K}}$ valley points.
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on DFT approximations, which may underestimate band gaps and magnetic moments compared to experiments.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate unit cells, stacking configurations, electrostatic potential variations ($\Delta V$), spin-polarized band dispersions showing splitting at K/$ ar{	ext{K}}$, and the evolution of band alignment under applied electric fields.
paper_structure: The paper details the crystal structure and methodology (DFT setup), presents results on emergent phenomena like altermagnetism, analyzes the tunability of band alignment via external fields, and concludes by establishing the material's potential for spintronics/valleytronics.
why_interesting: The ability to engineer multiple quantum functionalities (spin, valley, magnetism) simultaneously through symmetry control using electric fields is highly relevant for designing next-generation quantum devices and strongly correlated electronic materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The unit cell structures of the individual monolayers and their corresponding crystal field environments for MnPS3 and WS2 are illustrated here. Panels (a) and (b) show the optimized top and side views of the MnPS3 unit cell, respec- tively. MnPS3 forms a layered honeycomb lattice in which Mn and S atoms constitute tilted octahedra, while the P2 dimers form an inverted prism structure with surrounding S atoms, as depicted in (c). Similarly, (d) and (e) present the top and the side views of the WS2 unit cell after structure optimization. WS2 adopts a trigonal prismatic coordination, characteristic of the 2H-phase transition metal dichalcogenides, depicted in (f).

FIG. 2. The top view and the side view of the simulated MnPS3|WS2 heterostructure with stacking configuration I are depicted in (a) and (b), respectively. Similarly, (c), (d), and (e), (f) show the top and side views of stacking configuration II and III, respectively. The variation of the electrostatic potential energy along the z direction across the simulation cell is shown in (g), depicting the built-in potential difference in the heterostructure.

FIG. 3. The magnetic moment arrangements, spin-polarized, and orbital-projected band structures of MnPS3 and WS2 monolayers from our DFT calculations are presented here. Possible magnetic moment arrangements of MnPS3 are illustrated in (a), (b), (c), and (d), termed as zigzag-type AFM, N´eel-type AFM, stripy-type AFM, and ferromagnetic configurations, respectively. Panels (e) show the spin-polarized band dispersion of MnPS3 along the K1 →K2 path, with the inset showing the Brillouin zone, marking Γ, K1, K2, and Q-points. FIG. 4. Panels (a), (b), and (c) show the spin-polarized band dispersion of the heterostructure, for the stacking configurations I, II, and III, respectively, along the high-symmetry direction M →K →Γ →¯K →M from our DFT calculation. The band dispersion for three cases indicates a direct band gap ranging from 1.64 to 1.66 eV at the K and ¯K points. The inset of (b) shows the two-dimensional hexagonal Brillouin zone, marking the relevant high-symmetry points.

FIG. 5. The band dispersion with broken degeneracy along the K1 →Q →K2 path, as marked in the inset of Fig. 3(c), is shown here. Panels (a), (b), and (c) show the spin-polarized band dispersion of MnPS3|WS2 heterostructure for the stacking configurations I, II, and III, respectively, as obtained from our DFT calculations. These bands show that the opposite-spin bands from different sublattices are not degenerate, except at the Q-point.
